Kim/Monica/Jordan — quick note with the plan and deliverables.

Summary of approach:
- Break-glass event lifecycle: we create an immutable access pre-event at the time of the request that is written to a WORM-backed audit log; the access token is issued only after the pre-event write succeeds. The audit event includes a UUID, requester identity, timestamp, requested objects (IDs), business justification, and a short TTL for the elevated session.
- Tamper-evidence: audit logs are backed by append-only storage with SHA-256 chaining between blocks; we also keep signed manifests for 90 days to support external verification.
- Sample logs: Monica will attach a redacted sample with the exact fields Jordan asked for and a legend.

Deliverables and timeline:
- 4/13 EOD: one-page break-glass explainer (non-technical front; technical appendix) — owner: Rishi.
- 4/13 EOD: redacted sample logs + query to pull the same view from sandbox — owner: Monica.
- 4/15: short runbook for a break-glass drill (steps, success criteria, communications) + proposed drill dates — owner: Rishi/Monica.

Proposed privileged-access certification cadence:
- Recommend quarterly reviews for initial production rollout (lower friction), moving to monthly for >50 active privileged users. We can automate reviewer assignment and reminder emails via the Console — support for bulk certification exports exists today.

Meeting: Wed 4/13 9:30am PT works for us. I can do a 15–20 minute run-through of the sample logs and the pre-event behavior.

Action for Jordan/Alyssa: please confirm 9:30am PT and we will send calendar invite + a short agenda (log fields, break-glass lifecycle, certification options).
